subtitle: Lesson 21 · Pipeline-as-Code at Scale

steps.label: One good pipeline, copied everywhere
steps.sub: checkout, install, test, scan, build, deploy — pasted into every new repo

steps.label: Each copy drifts independently
steps.sub: one team adds caching, another skips the scan step and never restores it

steps.label: A fix means editing hundreds of files
steps.sub: nobody can say with confidence what pipeline behavior actually runs where

code:
# pipeline-templates repo: .github/workflows/build-test-scan.yml
name: Reusable Build, Test & Scan

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      node-version:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "20"
    secrets:
      NPM_TOKEN:
        required: true

jobs:
  build-test-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
      - name: Required security scan
        run: npm audit --audit-level=high
caption: on: workflow_call turns a normal workflow into one many repos can call.

eyebrow: Calling it from a consumer repo
code:
# consuming repo: .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI
on: [push]

jobs:
  run-shared-pipeline:
    uses: my-org/pipeline-templates/.github/workflows/build-test-scan.yml@v1
    with:
      node-version: "20"
    secrets:
      NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
caption: @v1, not @main — the consumer is pinned to a tagged release, not a moving target.

code:
resources:
  repositories:
    - repository: templates
      type: git
      name: PlatformEngineering/pipeline-templates
      ref: refs/tags/v1

extends:
  template: templates/build-test-scan.yml@templates
  parameters:
    nodeVersion: "20.x"
caption: extends means the consumer can't quietly skip the steps the template defines.
